findings: tests-miss-spec-behaviours (severity 2): the suite has 3 tests, all passing, but none covers the one-line output or --words, so a break in either passes it.
gain: The prototype has no test for the output line, for --words, or for the exit status on unreadable input, so a break in any of them passes the suite. Three tests through main() close that. Behaviours with a test go from 3 to 5: the specification's four bullets plus the project's exit-status standard.
delta: None. Output is stated in the opening sentence and example of the tool's specification, --words in its last bullet, and the exit status on unreadable input in the project's standards for every tool.

check: On v+1, all tests pass: test_output sees stdout '2 3 14\n' and return 0; test_words_option sees stdout '3\n' and return 0; test_unreadable_input sees return 2 and a non-empty stderr. Each test fails on a mutant of the tool's source: words joined by ',' instead of a space, --words ignored, and main() returning 0 on UnicodeDecodeError. Behaviours with a test: 5 of 5. The use case that grades whether every behaviour the specification names has a test rises from 0.7.

downsides.what: the rule 'every behaviour the specification names has a test' still has no enforcer

context: The tool reads a text on standard input and prints its lines, words and characters on one line, or only its words with --words; Python 3.9, standard library only. Its entry point main(argv) returns the exit status. The project's standards for every tool set exit status 2 when input cannot be read, here input that is not UTF-8. v is the prototype version before the change and v+1 the one after. A use case is a run graded from 0 to 1. A mutant is a copy of the tool's source with one behaviour broken on purpose.

pattern.context: A command-line tool is built from a specification, under project-wide standards such as exit codes, and has a unit-test suite.
pattern.problem: The tests call the inner functions, so behaviours at the program's edge (the output format, an option, the exit status on bad input) have no test. A break in any of them passes the suite.
pattern.solution: List each behaviour the specification and the project's standards name. Give each a test through the entry point, with standard input supplied and standard output and error captured. Break each behaviour once on purpose and see its test fail.
pattern.consequences: Every named behaviour has a test shown to catch its break, for a few lines of test code per behaviour. The rule that every named behaviour has a test is still kept by review, not by a tool.
